names.name: Powdered sugar
names.said: It goes everywhere. That is not a flaw in the product.

text.what: Sugar ground fine and cut with a little starch to stop it caking. The base of every glaze and the finish on beignets, malasadas and pączki.
text.story: Confectioner's sugar is graded by fineness — 10X is the finest common grade — and usually carries around 3 percent cornstarch as an anti-caking agent, which is why a glaze made from it sets opaque rather than clear.

kin.as: Where it is used by the bucket.

etymology.root: sugar ground to a powder; confectioner's sugar in the trade, icing sugar in Britain
etymology.note: Graded by fineness — 10X is the finest common grade — and cut with starch against caking.
